newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian government eyes Cineplex talks.
newsitem.headline: Canadian government eyes Cineplex talks.

text.p: Canada's Heritage Minister Sheila Copps wants to see more Canadian films in cinemas if merger talks between Cineplex Odeon Corp and Sony Corp unit Loews Theaters Group succeed, a government spokeswoman said on Monday.

"She would like to discuss with her colleague the Industry Minister (John) Manley what can be done to ensure that a greater quota of Canadian films are shown in whatever the exhibition conglomerate is," Copps' spokeswoman Janet Bax said in a telephone interview.

Foreign takeovers in Canada must be approved by government regulator Investment Canada, but a spokesman for Manley said the agency would not review the merger if the new company was dominated by Toronto-based Cineplex rather than Loews.
Cineplex confirmed on Friday that it was in discussions with Sony Retail Entertainment Inc about a possible merger that would create North America's second biggest movie theater chain.
The merged company would have 2,450 screens and rank just behind Carmike Cinemas Inc of Columbia, Ga., with 2,526 screens.
Cineplex's principal shareholders are Universal Studios Inc, a unit of Montreal-based Seagram Co Ltd and the Bronfman family, which is also the principal shareholder in Seagram.
